---
title: "Global hub and regional domains"
---

How several regional domains share one global solid Earth. The example is the science case of
[`par/kryos_NH-ANT-PAT_plastic_vilma2.nml`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/par/kryos_NH-ANT-PAT_plastic_vilma2.nml):
three plastic ice sheets (North on `NH-32KM`, Antarctica on `ANT-16KM`, PatagoniaPaleo on `PAT-PAL-8KM`) on VILMA2,
the global Earth `geo_glob` on its Gauss grid, with the rest of the world's ice from PaleoMIST's history. The general
structure of a run (instances, wiring, lags, clock) is on [Architecture](architecture.qmd); the backends are on
[VILMA2](backend-vilma2.md) and [PlasticIceSheet](backend-plastic.md); the runs themselves on
[Simulating our own ice](experiment-plastic.md).

The design is [`docs/dev/phase4-plan.md`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/docs/dev/phase4-plan.md) (sections 2-8); the code is
[`kryos_globe_ice.f90`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/src/core/kryos_globe_ice.f90) (the global ice field),
[`kryos_run_gia.f90`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/src/core/kryos_run_gia.f90) (its place in the
sequence) and
[`kryos_geo_vilma2.f90`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/src/backends/geo/kryos_geo_vilma2.f90) (the Earth and
its ports).

## The pieces

| Instance or group | Scope | Grid | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `geo_glob` | globe | `GAUSS-L170` (built by the backend) | the Earth: VILMA2's sea-level equation and viscoelastic response, on the host's loads |
| `[globe_ice]` | globe (a par group, not an instance) | `GLOBAL-0.5DEG` (background) | the background ice and bed X, the external ice history, the reference and the merges |
| `ice_nor`, `ice_ant`, `ice_pat` | domain | `NH-32KM`, `ANT-16KM`, `PAT-PAL-8KM` (their hubs) | the loads: plastic ice, gathered by the core |
| `geo_nor`, `geo_ant`, `geo_pat` | domain | the ice grid | the ports: the regional view of the global Earth, the bed and sea level back to the ice |

Three nested areas matter in every global field:

- the **footprint** of a domain: where its ice model holds ice (static; for the plastic backend the union of its
  margin slices). Inside it the load is the ice model's.
- the **host region**: the area covered by the domains' ice grids, with coverage `host_w` = `w` on the Gauss grid.
  Inside it, but outside the footprint, the ice is the external history interpolated to the ice grid, with the ice
  model's own flotation rule. The host region is where VILMA2 takes the host's terms.
- the rest of the globe, `1 − w`: the external ice on the Gauss grid, with VILMA2's own flotation and coastline rule.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph G ["globe"]
        X["[globe_ice]<br/>X at ext_tref<br/>+ history anomaly<br/>(GLOBAL-0.5DEG)"]
        GI["globe_ice<br/>reference, gather<br/>(merges)"]
        E["geo_glob<br/>VILMA2<br/>(GAUSS-L170)"]
    end
    subgraph DN ["domain North (NH-32KM)"]
        IN["ice_nor"]
        PN["geo_nor (port)"]
    end
    subgraph DA ["domain Antarctica (ANT-16KM)"]
        IA["ice_ant"]
        PA["geo_ant (port)"]
    end
    X --> GI
    IN -->|"H_ice, f_grnd, z_bed, z_sl<br/>lag 1"| GI
    IA --> GI
    GI -->|"H_ice_ext, host_w, host_Ig,<br/>host_C, host_F"| E
    E -->|"dz_bed, dz_ss (bilin),<br/>dphi, bsl; lag 0"| PN
    E --> PA
    PN -->|"z_bed = ref + dz_bed<br/>z_sl = dphi + dz_ss"| IN
    PA --> IA
```

PatagoniaPaleo (`ice_pat`, `geo_pat`) is a third domain of the same form.

## Grids and maps

| Grid | Where it comes from | Coupler |
|---|---|---|
| `GAUSS-L<lmax>` | built by the `vilma2` backend at `init`: `nlat = 2 lmax + 2`, `nphi = 4 lmax` (or `nlat`, `nphi` of `[vilma]`), longitudes from 0, the cell areas VILMA2's quadrature areas; its description is written to `<map_fldr>/grid_GAUSS-L<lmax>.txt` (an existing file is checked against it) | the globe's, and every domain's (`globe_register_grid`) |
| `GLOBAL-0.5DEG` | `[globe_ice] grid`, read from `grid_GLOBAL-0.5DEG.txt` of the map folder | the globe's |
| each domain's ice grid | `grid_<name>.txt` of the map folder; registered in the globe's coupler with the true (ellipsoidal) cell areas as model areas | the globe's and its domain's |

The globe has its own coupler (`globe%cpl`) on the map folder of `[kryos] map_fldr`. Both couplers cache their maps
in that folder, so it needs the grid descriptions of every grid of the run (the par file notes `grid_PAT-PAL-8KM.txt`
for Patagonia). VILMA2 stops if it does not recognise the grid as its own Gauss grid (it would build a remap).

The remaps of the global ice field:

| From → to | Method | What |
|---|---|---|
| background → Gauss | `con` | `z_bed` of X; the ice (X, then the external ice) as an amount per target area |
| background → ice grid | `con` | the external ice inside the host region (`ext_to_ice`) |
| ice grid → Gauss | merge (`coupler_merge_*`) | the host terms; `host_w` is the summed coverage |
| ice grid → background | merge | the spliced reference and the merged ice of `globe_ice.nc` |
| Gauss → port grid | `bilin` (domain's coupler) | the anomalies `dz_bed`, `dz_ss` |
| port grid → ice grid | `auto` | identity here (the port is on the ice grid) |

## The reference (`gia_reference`)

Once, after every instance's `PASS_INIT` and before the cold start or a restore. The ice instances have published
their static exports `footprint`, `H_ice_pd` and `z_bed_ref` (the domain's reference on the ice grid).

1. Each domain is registered in name order (`globe_ice_add_domain`): its ice grid, its statics, and its coverage and
   footprint fraction on the two global grids. Two domains on one ice grid, or a grid named like a global grid, stop.
2. Background X on the background grid (the datasrc of `[globe_ice] z_bed_ref`, `H_ice_ref` at `ext_tref`), remapped to
   the Gauss grid: `z_bed_ref`, `H_ice_ref` of `geo_glob` (VILMA2's reference for the `1 − w` part).
3. Per domain on its ice grid, with sea level 0 and the bed `z_bed_ref` in every cell:
   `H_tot = m·H_ice_pd + (1 − m)·X_i` (`m` the footprint, `X_i` the background ice on the ice grid),
   `f_g,ref = flot(H_tot, z_bed_ref, 0)` (the ice instance's flotation binding), `I = H_tot·f_g,ref`,
   `C = 1 − f_g,ref`, merged onto the Gauss grid: `host_w`, `host_Ig_ref`, `host_C_ref` (`F_ref = 0`).
4. The spliced reference on the background grid, `(1 − Σ f_d)·X + Σ f_d·ref_d` for the bed and the ice, for the
   hub output and the diagnostics. VILMA2 gets only the background part (item 2): the spliced ice would count a
   domain's present day twice in partial cells.

These five fields are put into `geo_glob`'s imports at `t0`; the Earth is then built at them (`PASS_GEOMETRY`:
`solid_earth_init`, exports zero). The log gives each domain's grounded ice, its footprint, and the ocean area of the
reference against the sea-surface area of the run's constants (a warning beyond 1 %).

## The gather (`gia_gather`)

At the start of a step when `geo_glob` is due, before its update, on the ice exports of the previous step (lag 1).

1. **Load time.** For every domain the `T_GIA` row into `host_w` is checked (`wire_lag_status`) against the ice's last
   update; that update is the load time `t_load`. Two domains whose ice was last updated at different times stop the
   run: the Earth has one load time.
2. **External ice** on the background grid: `H_ext = max(0, X + ΔH_hist(min(t_load, ext_tref)))` (`ext = "file"`;
   `"ref"`: X), the clipped mass logged; remapped to the Gauss grid: `H_ice_ext`. With X the history's own slice at
   `ext_tref`, `H_ext` is the history.
3. **Per domain** on its ice grid, the ice's `H_ice`, `f_grnd`, `z_bed`, `z_sl` (the bed and sea level the ice used)
   and `footprint`:

   ```
   H_tot = m·H + (1 − m)·ext_i
   f_g   = m·f_grnd + (1 − m)·flot(H_tot, z_bed, z_sl)
   I = H_tot·f_g,   C = 1 − f_g,   F = z_bed_ref·(f_g,ref − f_g)
   ```

   merged onto the Gauss grid (`I` and `F` extensive, `C` intensive), with the same procedure as the reference.
4. **Checks.** The footprint must equal the registered one and `host_w` the reference's; `host_w` is clipped to
   `[0, 1]` and `host_C` to `[0, host_w]` (round-off of the conservative maps; an excess above 1e-6 stops); finite
   values, `host_Ig ≥ 0`; the merged grounded ice and the external ice are conserved to `cons_tol` (1e-9).
5. **Log**: per domain and for the external ice, the change of grounded volume against the reference as sea-level
   equivalent `−(ρ_i/ρ_w) ΔV / A`, the clipped external mass and the merge closure.
6. `H_ice_ext`, `host_w`, `host_Ig`, `host_C`, `host_F` are put into `geo_glob`'s imports with validity `t_load`.

The `T_GIA` rows of the wiring table exist for resolution, logging and the lag check; the exchange never runs them.
The arithmetic is the core's, because it needs the flotation, the external ice and the merge.

## The Earth (`geo_glob`)

VILMA2 computes in `real64`; the adapter only hands the imports to VILMA2 and puts what it returns.

| Import | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `H_ice_ext` | external ice, mean over the `1 − w` part |
| `host_w` | coverage of the host region |
| `host_Ig` | grounded-ice column `w·H·f_g` |
| `host_C` | ocean fraction `w·(1 − f_g)` |
| `host_F` | flooded-area fill `w·ζ⁽⁰⁾·(C − C_ref)` |
| `z_bed_ref`, `H_ice_ref`, `host_Ig_ref`, `host_C_ref` | the reference (static) |

| Export | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dz_bed` | bed change |
| `dz_ss` | sea-surface change relative to `dphi` (VILMA2's `dz_ss − dphi`) |
| `dphi` | the uniform sea-surface shift |
| `bsl` | barystatic sea level, the ocean mean of `C·rsl` |
| `C_ocn` | total ocean function (diagnostic) |
| `bsl_ive`, `bsl_ive_host` | ice-volume equivalent and its host part (diagnostics) |
| `A_ocn` | `∫ C dA` |
| `mass_resid` | worst sea-level-equation mass residual of the step |

`update`: `solid_earth_update(se, H_ice_ext, t1 − t0, host_w, host_Ig, host_C, host_F)`. VILMA2 ramps the load
linearly from the previous call's to this one. The densities are the run's (`phys_const`: `rho_ice`, `rho_sw`), set
into VILMA2 at `init` and logged.

## Sea level and ocean function

Inside the host region VILMA2's sea-level solve uses the host's terms; on `1 − w` it applies its own flotation and
coastline rule to `H_ice_ext` (VILMA2 README, "Host-resolved terms"). So the grounding of every load cell in a domain
is the ice model's: its own `f_grnd` inside the footprint, its `flotation` binding with its own densities outside
(plastic: grounded where `ρ_i H ≥ ρ_w (z_sl − z_bed)`).

The sea level the ice sees is `z_sl = dphi + dz_ss`, of this step (lag 0). `bsl` reaches every port as a scalar and
is a diagnostic there; `rsl = dz_ss + dphi − dz_bed` is a diagnostic of the output, not an export. The ocean
function `C_ocn` and `bsl_ive` are written by `geo_glob`, and VILMA2's own file (`out_vilma`) has `rsl`, `bsl`,
`bsl_ive`.

## The ports and the scatter

A port (`vilma_geo_t`, `geo_nor`, `geo_ant`, `geo_pat`) is stateless. It has no `H_ice` import (the row ice → geo
`H_ice` is inactive) and no `dV_bsl`, so `reduce_bsl` finds no source and returns.

1. Rows `geo_g → geo`, run by `bsl_to_geo` when the port is due: `dz_bed`, `dz_ss` (bilinear from the Gauss grid to
   the port grid, in the domain's coupler; anomalies stay anomalies), `dphi`, `bsl`.
2. The port's `update` copies these imports to its exports with their validity, and its `z_bed_ref` import (from the
   ice, static) to its export, which `domain_check_reference` compares with the domain's reference.
3. In block 4 of the step, `exchange_into(ice)` runs the rows geo → ice:
   `z_bed = z_bed_ref(ice grid) + dz_bed` (`T_ADD_REF`) and `z_sl = dphi + dz_ss` (`T_ADD_SCALAR`), both `auto`, lag 0.

The bed the ice sees is therefore the domain's reference topography plus the Earth's anomaly, remapped once (Gauss →
ice grid). The hub follows through the ice (`domain_hub_update`).

## The reference topography (refcorr)

A glacial-cycle run that starts from equilibrium under the initial load needs a reference bed that is today's bed plus
the rebound still to come at the end of the run, so that the run ends on today's bed instead of one too deep under the
former ice sheets ([`docs/dev/vilma2-paleomist.md`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/docs/dev/vilma2-paleomist.md), "The iterated reference", "Present-day reference correction for
kryos"). The correction `r` enters kryos only through the reference topography, shared by every component; no source
code is involved.

| Par group | File | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `[topo_nor]`, `[topo_ant]`, `[topo_pat]` `path` | `kryos_data/refcorr/PaleoMIST-sci/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_TOPO-<source>-refcorr.nc` | the domain topography with `z_bed + r`, `z_srf` moved with it, the other variables unchanged |
| `[X_z_bed]`, `[X_H_ice]` `filename` (`mode = "static"`) | `kryos_data/refcorr/PaleoMIST-sci/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_REFCORR.nc` | the history's 0 ka bed + `r`, its 0 ka ice |

`H_ice` stays present-day. The hub prepares the corrected reference; every instance grid's reference comes from it,
and the global reference is the merge of the domains' references with X.

The tool is [`tools/levante/gia_refcorr.sh`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/tools/levante/gia_refcorr.sh)
(with `gia_refcorr.jl`, `gia_refcorr_plot.jl`): standalone VILMA2 (`$VILMA2/bin/vilma.x`; the published cases used the
gate stack S11) with the `&vilma` group of a
kryos par file and the run's densities, under a FesmData ice history, iterated with `i_eq = 3` as
`r_{n+1} = rsl_n(0 ka)` from `r_0 = 0` until `max |r_n − rsl_n(0 ka)| < TOL` (default 1.5 m, at most `NMAX = 8` runs).
It writes the reference files under `$KRYOS_WORK/kryos_data/refcorr/<CASE>/` (`KD` overrides the parent; domains from
`DOMAINS`, `"<domain>:<hub grid>:<topo file under fesmdata> ..."`, default North and Antarctica), and is restartable per
iteration (the case folder is a PaleoMIST runme project, `tools/levante/pm_project.sh` with `pm_data` -> its
`data/`; each iteration `it<n>` is a runme run of its `vilma_rc.nml`, rerun unless its `status` is 0). It submits
itself (shared partition, 2 days, 128 cpus, 60 GB) and runs the iterations within that job:

```bash
CASE=PaleoMIST-sci PAR=<kryos par file> tools/levante/gia_refcorr.sh
```

A run reads the case through its `kryos_data` link, runme's copy of the checkout's: point that link at
`$KRYOS_WORK/kryos_data` (remove it, set `KRYOS_DATA` and rerun `tools/levante/setup.sh`), or copy the case into the
shared `/work/ba1442/kryos_data`, where the published cases are.

For the science case (3-D Earth, PaleoMIST 80 → 0 ka linear in time, ρ_i 910, ρ_w 1028) it converged in 4 runs to a
0 ka bed misfit of 0.23 m; `r` reaches 396 m over Quebec-Labrador and 126 m under the Ronne-Filchner ice, 24 m RMS
globally ([`docs/dev/vilma2-paleomist.md`](https://github.com/fesmc/kryos/blob/main/docs/dev/vilma2-paleomist.md)). Limits: `r` is computed with the history's own 0 ka bed as VILMA2's
reference, not with the kryos merge of the domain topographies, and with the history's ice, not the ice the coupled
run produces; one more fixed-point step from the coupled run's own 0 ka `rsl` refreshes it (`gia_refcorr.jl next`).
Another Earth or history needs its own case.

The PatagoniaPaleo topography `[topo_pat]` names,
`kryos_data/refcorr/PaleoMIST-sci/PatagoniaPaleo/PAT-PAL-8KM/PAT-PAL-8KM_TOPO-GEBCO2026-refcorr.nc`, was made on
2026-11-09 with `gia_refcorr.jl write` on the converged `r.nc` of PaleoMIST-sci (no new GIA run), domain spec
`PatagoniaPaleo:PAT-PAL-8KM:<fesmdata>/PatagoniaPaleo/PAT-PAL-8KM/PAT-PAL-8KM_TOPO-GEBCO2026.nc`. Any domain can be
added to a case this way, or with `DOMAINS` when running `gia_refcorr.sh`:

```bash
julia --project=tools/levante tools/levante/gia_refcorr.jl write <r.nc> <out folder> <X grid>:<history on that grid> <domain>:<hub grid>:<topo file> ...
```

runme links `kryos_data` into every run folder from the checkout's link (`.runme/info.json` links input, fesmdata,
kryos_data, maps, ice_data and isostasy_data; `tools/levante/setup.sh` makes `kryos_data -> $KRYOS_DATA`).

## Cadence and time constraints

- **One cadence for the Earth and its ports.** A port takes the `dt`, `phase` and `clock` of `geo_glob`
  (`domain_create(..., port_dt, port_phase, port_clock)`); a port group that sets another `dt` stops (`gia_check`).
  The science case sets `dt = 100` in all four groups, with `dtt = 100`.
- **One ice cadence across the domains.** The gather stops when two domains' ice were last updated at different
  times.
- **Lag.** The Earth's call at step `n` takes the ice of step `n − 1` (lag 1), so VILMA2's load history is one geo
  interval behind the ice; the ice takes the Earth's solution of this step (lag 0).
- **Spin-up.** `gia_check` stops a run whose `[vilma]` has no spin-up (`pre_spinup_1d`, or `equil_time_max > 0`) unless
  `geo_glob` sets `allow_no_spinup = True`: the `dt = 0` seed solves the previous load, so without a spin-up the t0 load
  would enter with the first call.
- **Fixed footprint and coverage.** The footprints and the grids are fixed for the run; a change stops the gather.
- **No overlap.** The domains are registered without priorities, so their grids must not overlap on the global grids
  (a coverage above `1 + overlap_tol` stops).
- **The history's range.** `[X_dH_ice]` must be `mode = "transient"`, `anomaly_ref = "slice"`, `ref_time = ext_tref`,
  `out_of_range = "error"`; the gather holds it at `ext_tref` after that time, and a run before its first record stops.
- **Combinations.** `vilma2` on the globe and in the domains go together; every domain needs an ice instance with
  `flotation`, `footprint` and `H_ice_pd`; FastIsostasy with VILMA2 stops (not implemented).
- Restart times and `time_end` must lie on every cadence grid (`clock_start`).

## Step by step

### Cold start

1. `PASS_INIT` of every instance: the ice publishes `footprint`, `H_ice_pd`, `z_bed_ref`; the static rows put the ice's
   `z_bed_ref`, `H_ice_ref` into the ports.
2. `gia_reference`; `geo_glob` `PASS_GEOMETRY` (VILMA2 built at the reference, exports zero).
3. Per domain: rows into the port (zero anomalies), port `PASS_GEOMETRY`, `domain_check_reference`; rows geo → ice,
   ice `PASS_GEOMETRY`. The boundary and the ice state (`PASS_STATE`, `PASS_SPINUP`) are made on the reference bed.
4. `gia_seed`: the gather at `t0` (the final initial ice), `geo_glob` `PASS_STATE` (VILMA2's spin-up holding the t0
   load: the 1-D pre-spin-up, then the full model to `equil_rate_tol` or at most `equil_time_max`; then the `dt = 0`
   seed), the rows into the ports, port `PASS_STATE`.
5. Per domain: rows geo → ice and ice `PASS_GEOMETRY` again (the bed and sea level of the seed), the hub, and a last
   surface cycle when the domain has a surface.

### One step `t_{n−1} → t_n`

1. `gia_gather`: the ice of `t_{n−1}`, merged with the external ice at `t_{n−1}` into the host terms.
2. `geo_glob` update: VILMA2 from `t_{n−1}` to `t_n`; exports at `t_n`.
3. Per domain, the port: `dz_bed`, `dz_ss` remapped to the ice grid, `dphi`, `bsl`; the port's update.
4. Per domain: the ice gets `z_bed = z_bed_ref + dz_bed` and `z_sl = dphi + dz_ss`, and solves at `t_n` (plastic:
   the margin and `tau_b` at `t_n` on that bed and sea level); the hub follows.
5. The ice exports of `t_n` are the load of the next gather.

### Restore

`gia_reference` rebuilds the reference from the files and the static exports, `geo_glob` `PASS_GEOMETRY` builds
VILMA2 at it, and the restore reads `geo_glob_restart.nc` (`vilma_restart_read`: it checks the reference against the
model just built and restores the memory, the rotation and the ramp's last host terms), then `geo_glob`'s imports and
exports. The ports are stateless: their imports and exports are the bundle's, and no row runs for them. The global ice
field is not stored; nothing is gathered or stepped. A chunked run equals the continuous run bit for bit
(`tests/test_gia_sequence.f90`).

## Configuration

```fortran
&globe
    geo = "geo_glob"
/
&geo_glob
    backend         = "vilma2"
    grid            = ""                 ! the Gauss grid GAUSS-L<lmax>, built by the backend
    dt              = 100.0              ! [yr] cadence of the Earth
    clock           = "model"
    vilma           = "vilma"            ! the &vilma group (overrides of input/vilma_defaults.nml)
    ice_bg          = "globe_ice"        ! the global ice field group
    allow_no_spinup = False
    out_2D          = "out_2D"           ! dz_bed, dz_ss, C_ocn on lon, lat
    out_1D          = "out_1D"
    out_gia         = "none"             ! geo_glob_gia.nc: the host imports as VILMA2 got them
    out_vilma       = "out_2D"           ! geo_glob_vilma.nc: VILMA2's own diagnostics
/
&globe_ice
    grid      = "GLOBAL-0.5DEG"          ! background grid
    z_bed_ref = "X_z_bed"                ! background bed X at ext_tref
    H_ice_ref = "X_H_ice"                ! background ice X at ext_tref
    ext       = "file"                   ! ice outside the footprints: X + the history's anomaly
    ext_field = "X_dH_ice"
    ext_tref  = 0.0                      ! [yr] model time of the history's present day
    out_2D    = "none"                   ! schedule of globe_ice.nc
/
&X_dH_ice
    filename     = "fesmdata/Global/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_IceHistory-PaleoMIST.nc"
    name         = "H_ice"
    mode         = "transient"
    anomaly_ref  = "slice"
    ref_time     = 0.0                   ! = ext_tref
    out_of_range = "error"
/
&geo_nor
    backend = "vilma2"
    grid    = "NH-32KM"                  ! the ice grid
    dt      = 100.0                      ! the cadence of geo_glob (a different value stops)
/
```

`[globe_ice]` also has `target` (the global grid of the host terms without VILMA2, below), `overlap_tol` (0.01) and
`cons_tol` (1e-9). All keys: [Par files](reference-par-files.md).

## Output

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `geo_glob.nc`, `geo_glob_ts.nc` | the Earth's exports on `lon`, `lat` (`dz_bed`, `dz_ss`, `C_ocn`), and its 0-D series (`dphi`, `bsl`, `bsl_ive`, `A_ocn`, `mass_resid`, ...) |
| `geo_glob_vilma.nc` | VILMA2's own diagnostics (`rsl`, `bsl`, `bsl_ive`; what the GAPSLIP scores read) |
| `geo_glob_gia.nc` | the host imports as VILMA2 got them, and `t_load` (`out_gia`) |
| `geo_nor.nc`, `geo_nor_ts.nc`, ... | the ports' exports on the ice grids |
| `globe_ice.nc` | the global geometry hub on the background grid: the spliced reference `z_bed_ref`, `H_ice_ref` and the coverage `cov` (static), the merged ice `H_ice` of the last gather and `t_load` |

Precisions: `input/kryos-variables-geo.md`, `kryos-variables-geo-vilma2.md`, `kryos-variables-globe_ice.md`.

## Without VILMA2: the observing hub

`[globe_ice]` in a run without a host-resolved geo (e.g. FastIsostasy domains) builds the same reference and merged
ice on the grid named by `[globe_ice] target` (a `grid_<name>.txt` of the map folder) and writes `globe_ice.nc`;
nothing feeds back. The gather then runs every step (or on the global geo's cadence), the ice checks of `gia_check`
apply, and the run is bit-identical to the same run without the group.
